title: Signaling for Rescue
content:
Rescue often depends on being seen or heard. Signal early, while you have energy, and use the most far-reaching method available.

Universal distress signals come in threes: three fires, three whistle blasts, three flashes. Three of anything, evenly spaced, reads as a deliberate call for help.

Visual signals:
- Fire and smoke. By night, fire is visible for miles. By day, add green vegetation to a fire to make thick white smoke (or oil/rubber for dark smoke against snow).
- Signal mirror or any reflective surface. Aimed sun flashes can be seen for many miles, even from aircraft. Sweep the horizon and flash toward any vehicle, plane, or person.
- Ground-to-air symbols stamped in snow or laid out with rocks/logs: a large 'V' means require assistance, 'X' means require medical assistance. Make them huge and high-contrast.
- Bright clothing or gear spread in the open.

Audio signals:
- A whistle carries far longer than your voice and saves energy. Three blasts, pause, repeat.

Stay put once you have signaled, if it is safe to do so. A stationary person near a visible signal is far easier to find than a moving one.
